title: Tenant-weighted embedding onboarding with staged fallbacks and quality fences
creator: Aisha Bennett
description:
Background:
We need a predictable, low-risk mechanism to onboard new embedding models (and model variants used by the reranker pipeline) while preserving quality and latency SLAs for existing tenants. Previous onboarding flows relied on uniform traffic splits and binary canaries; those approaches caused occasional tenant-visible quality regressions for high-sensitivity customers and didn't protect tail latency when under load.

Goal:
- Allow gradual, tenant-weighted activation of a new embedding variant with independent controls for quality gating (semantic regression) and latency gating (p95 threshold).
- Provide automatic, fast rollback to pinned variants when customer-facing thresholds are breached.
- Produce reliable telemetry (per-tenant and aggregated) to drive automated roll-forward decisions and postmortems.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to embeddings and the reranking endpoint that consumes embeddings (embedding+rerank flow).
- Must work across Hosted and Dedicated deployments; Private deployments should be supported but may need separate rollout mechanics (documented as follow-up).
- No storage schema migration; use existing model aliasing and variant metadata services.

Design summary:
1) Tenant-weighted mirror: new variant starts in mirror/shadow mode for a configurable set of tenants, collecting full telemetry without influencing user-facing responses.
2) Graduated activation: per-tenant weight values (0% -> 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) applied on a cadence (e.g., 24h per step) and only advanced if health gates pass.
3) Quality fences: automated checks comparing rerank/recall metrics (R@k, MRR proxy, embedding-cosine-distribution drift score) between baseline and candidate. A small cohort of synthetic evaluation queries (seeded via eval harness) runs each step to produce a delta.
4) Latency fences: p50/p95/p99 and CPU/GPU inference time per request must remain within configured delta of baseline (default: p95 increase <= 15%).
5) Automatic fallbacks: if either fence fails for a tenant, weight is reduced to prior safe level or the tenant is pinned back to baseline and an alert + replay rate-limited job is created for developers.
6) Telemetry ownership: the onboarding flow emits a per-tenant onboarding record (variant, weight, step_ts, gate_results) retained for 30d for audits and debugging.

Why tenant-weighted vs cohort-only?
Some customers are hypersensitive (search SaaS with high manual review volume). Tenant-weighted activation lets us target lower-risk tenants early while protecting high-risk ones. It also enables per-tenant rollback without disrupting global rollout progress.
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding UI/CLI: ability to start a tenant-weighted onboarding run that lists target tenants and initial weights.
Shadow mode collects full telemetry for selected tenants without changing their responses.
Automated gates run at each step and either advance or revert weight according to configured thresholds.
Per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU time, and embedding cosine-drift metrics are visible in Console dashboards for the onboarding run.
System can perform automatic tenant-level rollback and generates an incident artifact with replay instructions.
Load test demonstrates no more than 10% increase in overall tail latency when onboarding up to 50% of tenants simultaneously (on our staging cluster).
Documentation (Runbook + design doc) published and linked from the Console onboarding UI.
runbook: Start onboarding: POST /admin/onboard-embedding with model_alias, tenant_list, initial_weight, step_interval
Monitor Console onboarding dashboard: check gating table and heatmaps (quality delta, latency delta, resource utilization)
If a gate trips for a tenant: either pause progression for that tenant or set weight back to previous step via admin API
To rollback globally: call /admin/onboard-embedding/cancel which pins all affected tenants to baseline and triggers a replay job for failed queries
For emergency hotfix: update alias mapping to revert candidate variant immediately and open a P0 incident referencing onboarding id
telemetry_signals: embedding.cosine_drift.mean_delta (candidate vs baseline over seed eval set)
rollout_plan: Phase A (Shadow, 48h): Mirror traffic for 5 low-risk tenants and collect telemetry; run automated seed-eval every 4h
Phase B (Micro canary, 72h): Activate 1% weight for 20 additional tenants; monitor gates hourly; auto rollback on gate breach
Phase C (Broad gradual, 7d): Step weights 1% -> 10% -> 50% with 24h minimum per step for approved tenants
Phase D (Full cutover): Close-out monitoring for 7 days and mark candidate as recommended in model catalog; schedule deprecation of old variant per policy
